question: Should the final mutation guards and deferred state-token renewal ship together now, with any freshness uncertainty blocking authoritative repair writes and publication?
rationale: The implementation is coherent and policy-aligned, but it changes failure behavior across close, merge, comment, label, receipt, and state-publication boundaries; only maintainers can accept that operational rollout tradeoff.

options.title: Stage and monitor together
options.body: Approve the combined fail-closed guards and credential renewal, then monitor a controlled live repair run for rejected and successful mutation receipts.

options.title: Split credential renewal
options.body: Land the mutation-boundary guards first and defer workflow credential rebinding if maintainers want a smaller operational rollout.

options.title: Hold for more canary proof
options.body: Keep the draft open until a controlled repair run demonstrates both stale rejection and unaffected successful post-flight publication.

recommendation.title: Stage and monitor together
recommendation.body: Approve the combined fail-closed guards and credential renewal, then monitor a controlled live repair run for rejected and successful mutation receipts.

likelyOwner.reason: His prior work spans the repair workflow, mutation locks, and state-publication integration where the rollout tradeoff is concentrated.
